title: Antinous is no match for Jesus
source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτα καὶ τὰ περὶ τῶν παιδικῶν Ἀδριανοῦ (λέγω δὲ τὰ περὶ Ἀντινόου τοῦ μειρακίου καὶ τὰς εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν ἐν Ἀντινόου (πόλει) τῆς Αἰγύπτου τιμὰς) οὐδὲν οἴεται ἀποδεῖν τῆς ἡμετέρας πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν τιμῆς, φέρε καὶ τοῦτο ὡς φιλέχθρως λεγόμενον διελέγξωμεν. τί γὰρ κοινὸν ἔχει ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τοῖς Ἀδριανοῦ παιδικοῖς βίος, οὐδὲ τὸν ἄῤῥενα ἀπαθῇ γυναικείας νόσου φυλάξαντος. πρὸς τὸν σεμνὸν ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν, οὗ μηδὲ οἱ μυρία κατηγορήσαντες καὶ ψευδῆ ὅσα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες δεδύνηνται κατειπεῖν ὡς κἂν τὸ τυχὸν ἀκολασίας κἂν ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον γευσαμένου; ἀλλὰ καὶ εἴπερ φιλαλήθως καὶ ἀδεκάστως τὰ περὶ τὸν Ἀντίνου ἐξετάζοι τις, μαγγανείας ἂν Αἰγυπτίων καὶ τελετὰς εὕροι τὰς αἰτίας τοῦ δοκεῖν τι αὐτὸν ποιεῖν ἐν Ἀντινόου πόλει καὶ μετὰ τὴν τελευτὴν αὐτοῦ· ὅπερ καὶ ἐπ᾿ ἄλλων νεὼν ἱστορεῖται ὑπὸ Αἰγυπτίων καὶ τῶν τὰ τοιαῦτα δεινῶν γεγονέναι, ἔν τισι τόποις ἱδρυόντων δαίμονας μαντικοὺς ἢ ἰατρικοὺς πολλάκις δὲ καὶ βασανίζοντας τοὺς δοκοῦντάς τι παραβεβηκέναι περὶ τῶν τυχόντων βρωμάτων ἢ περὶ τοῦ θιγεῖν νεκροῦ σώματος ἀνθρωπίνου, ἵνα δοκοῖεν δεδίττεσθαι τὸν πολὺν καὶ ἀπαίδευτον. τοιοῦτος δέ ἐστι καὶ ἐν Ἀντινόου πόλει τῆς Αἰγύπτου νομισθεὶς εἶναι θεὸς, οὗ ἀρετὰς οἱ μέν τινες κυβευτικώτερον ζῶντες καταψεύδονται, ἕτεροι δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐκεῖ ἱδρυμένου δαίμονος ἀπατώμενοι καὶ ἄλλοι ἀπὸ ἀσθενοῦς τοῦ συνειδότος ἐλεγχόμενοι οἴονται τίνειν θεήλατον ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀντινόου ποινήν. τοιαῦτα δέ ἐστι καὶ τὰ δρώμενα αὐτῶν μυστήρια καὶ αἱ δοκοῦσαι μαντεῖαι, ων πάνυ μακράν ἐστι τὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. οὐ γὰρ συνελθόντες γόητες, χάριν τίνοντες βασιλεῖ τινι κελεύοντι ἢ ἡγεμόνι προστάσσοντι, πεποιηκέναι ἔδοξαν αὐτὸν εἶναι θεὸν, ἀλλ᾿ αὐτὸς ὁ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργὸς ἀκολούθως τῇ ἐν τῷ λέγειν τεραστίως πιστικῇ δυνάμει συνέστησεν αὐτὸν ὡς τιμῆς ἄξιον οὐ τοῖς εὐφρονεῖν ἐθέλουσι μόνον ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ καὶ δαίμοσι καὶ ἄλλαις ἀοράτοις δυνάμεσιν· αἵτινες μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο ἐμφαίνουσιν ἤτοι φοβούμεναι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὡς κρείττονος ἤ σεβασμίως ἀποδεχόμεναι ὡς κατὰ νόμους αὐτῶν ἄρχοντος. εἰ γὰρ μὴ θεόθεν ἦν αὐτῷ δοθεῖσα σύστασις, οὐκ ἂν καὶ δαίμονες τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἀπαγγελλομένῳ μόνον εἴκοντες ἀνεχώρουν ἀπὸ τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν πολεμουμένων.
pass_a_gloss: But since after these he thinks the things about Hadrian’s darling (τὰ παιδικά, boy-favourite) (I mean the things about Antinous the lad (μειράκιον) and the honours (τιμαί) to him of those in Antinous’s [city] of Egypt) to fall short (ἀποδέω) in nothing of our honour toward Jesus, come, let us refute (διελέγχω) this also as said out of enmity (φιλέχθρως). For what in common (κοινόν) has the life (βίος) that came to be among Hadrian’s favourites, [of one] not even keeping (φυλάσσω) the male (ὁ ἄρρην) free from (ἀπαθής) womanly disease (γυναικεία νόσος), with our venerable (σεμνός) Jesus, of whom not even those who made countless accusations (κατηγορέω) and saying whatever lies (ψευδῆ) about him have been able to allege (κατειπεῖν) as having tasted (γεύομαι) even the slightest (τὸ τυχόν) licentiousness (ἀκολασία) even for a little [while]? But also, if with love of truth and impartially (ἀδεκάστως) anyone should examine the things about Antinous, he would find sorceries (μαγγανεῖαι) of Egyptians and rites (τελεταί) [to be] the causes of his seeming to do something in Antinous’s city even after his death (τελευτή); which also in the case of other temples is reported by Egyptians and those clever (δεινοί) at such things to have happened, establishing (ἱδρύω) in certain places demons prophetic (μαντικοί) or healing (ἰατρικοί), and often also tormenting (βασανίζω) those seeming to have transgressed (παραβαίνω) about ordinary/certain foods (βρώματα) or about touching (θιγγάνω) a dead (νεκρός) human body, that they might seem (δοκέω) to frighten (δεδίττομαι) the many and uneducated (ἀπαίδευτος). And such is also the one in Antinous’s city of Egypt considered (νομίζω) to be a god, whose virtues/miracles (ἀρεταί) some, living more like dice-players/cheats (κυβευτικώτερον), falsely allege (καταψεύδομαι), while others deceived (ἀπατάω) by the demon established there, and others convicted (ἐλέγχω) by a weak (ἀσθενής) conscience (τὸ συνειδός), think they are paying (τίνω) a god-driven (θεήλατος) penalty (ποινή) from Antinous. And such also are their mysteries (μυστήρια) performed (δράω) and the seeming oracles (μαντεῖαι), from which very far (πάνυ μακράν) are the things of Jesus. For not sorcerers (γόητες) having come together, paying a favour (χάριν τίνοντες) to some king ordering (κελεύω) or governor (ἡγεμών) commanding (προστάσσω), seemed to have made him to be a god, but the very craftsman (δημιουργός) of the wholes (τὰ ὅλα) himself, in accord (ἀκολούθως) with the marvellously (τεραστίως) persuasive (πιστικός) power (δύναμις) in speaking (τὸ λέγειν), commended (συνίστημι) him as worthy of honour not only to men wishing to be right-minded (εὐφρονέω) but also to demons and other invisible powers (ἀόρατοι δυνάμεις); which up to now (μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο) show (ἐμφαίνω) either fearing (φοβέομαι) the name of Jesus as stronger or reverently (σεβασμίως) accepting (ἀποδέχομαι) [him] as ruling (ἄρχω) according to their laws (νόμοι). For if the commendation (σύστασις) had not been given to him from God (θεόθεν), the demons would not, yielding (εἴκω) only to his name being pronounced (ἀπαγγέλλω), withdraw (ἀναχωρέω) from those warred upon (πολεμέω) by them.
pass_b_english: After this Celsus thinks that the story of Hadrian’s favourite (I mean the story of the youth Antinous, and the honours paid him by the people of the city of Antinous in Egypt) falls in no way short of the honour we pay to Jesus. Come, then, let us refute this too, as something said out of spite. For what has the life lived as the favourite of Hadrian, who did not even keep the male youth free from womanish disorder, in common with our revered Jesus? Even those who brought countless accusations against him and told every kind of lie about him have not been able to charge him with tasting even the least licentiousness, even for a short time.

Moreover, if anyone were to examine the facts about Antinous with a love of truth and without partiality, he would find that the sorceries and rites of the Egyptians are the causes of his seeming to do something in the city of Antinous even after his death. The same is reported to have been done in the case of other temples by Egyptians and by those skilled in such matters, who settle in certain places demons that give oracles or heal, and that often also torment those who seem to have transgressed in the matter of ordinary foods or of touching a dead human body, so that they may seem to strike fear into the uneducated multitude. Such too is the one who has come to be thought a god in the city of Antinous in Egypt. Some people, who live rather like cheats, invent false tales of his mighty deeds; others, deceived by the demon settled there, and others again, convicted by a weak conscience, suppose that they are paying a penalty sent by a god from Antinous. Such too are the mysteries they perform and their supposed oracles, from which the things of Jesus are very far removed.

For it was not sorcerers, coming together to repay a favour to some king who gave orders or some governor who commanded it, who were thought to have made him a god. It was the Maker of the universe himself who, in keeping with the marvellously persuasive power in his speaking, commended him as worthy of honour, not only to men who are willing to be of sound mind, but also to demons and other invisible powers. To this day these show either that they fear the name of Jesus as stronger than they, or that they reverently accept him as their lawful ruler. For if his commendation had not been given him by God, the demons too would not withdraw from those they assail, yielding at the mere pronouncing of his name.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 36 (Koetschau 3.36). Celsus’s comparison is reported indirectly (οἴεται ἀποδεῖν, infinitive) and is left without quotation marks. ‘(πόλει)’ in ‘ἐν Ἀντινόου (πόλει)’ is an editorial supplement and is translated (‘the city of Antinous’, i.e. Antinoopolis). The staged text has ‘Ἀντίνου’ once for ‘Ἀντινόου’; read as the same name. ‘τὰ παιδικά’ rendered ‘favourite’ (the boy-beloved); ‘ἐν τοῖς Ἀδριανοῦ παιδικοῖς’ names the role (‘lived as the favourite of Hadrian’), not a group of favourites. ‘οὐδὲ τὸν ἄρρενα ἀπαθῆ γυναικείας νόσου φυλάξαντος’ rendered ‘who did not even keep the male youth free from womanish disorder’: the genitive participle agrees with the nearest genitive, Ἀδριανοῦ (βίος is nominative), so Hadrian is the one who did not keep the youth from the passive part in a male relationship; ‘τὸν ἄρρενα’ (the male) is the youth, and ‘youth’ comes from ‘μειράκιον’ above. ‘νόσος’ (disease) is softened to ‘disorder’ to keep the dignified register without changing the sense. ‘σεμνός’ rendered ‘revered’ (venerable, grave); ‘holy’ is kept for ἅγιος. ‘κἂν τὸ τυχὸν ἀκολασίας κἂν ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον’ = ‘even the least licentiousness, even for a short time’; both ‘even’s kept. ‘περὶ τῶν τυχόντων βρωμάτων’ rendered ‘ordinary foods’ (τυχών, any commonplace thing; compare ‘τὸ τυχὸν ἀκολασίας’, ‘the least licentiousness’, above): Origen scorns torments over trivial matters. ‘ἵνα δοκοῖεν δεδίττεσθαι’: the subject may be the demons or those who settle them; left as ‘they’, as in the Greek. ‘ἀρεταί’ here means wonders or mighty deeds (as in aretalogy), not moral virtues; rendered ‘mighty deeds’. ‘κυβευτικώτερον ζῶντες’ (living more like dice-players, i.e. tricksters) rendered ‘who live rather like cheats’. ‘ἀπὸ ἀσθενοῦς τοῦ συνειδότος’ may echo Paul’s ‘weak conscience’ (1 Corinthians 8:7, 10, 12), but the phrase is common and the echo uncertain; not cited inline. ‘ὁ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργός’ rendered ‘the Maker of the universe’ (God), capitalised. ‘τῇ ἐν τῷ λέγειν τεραστίως πιστικῇ δυνάμει’ is taken as the persuasive power of Jesus’ speaking (the commendation is ‘in keeping with’ it). ‘ὡς κατὰ νόμους αὐτῶν ἄρχοντος’ rendered ‘as their lawful ruler’ (ruling them according to laws). The subjection of demons and invisible powers may recall Philippians 2:10 or Colossians 2:15, but no wording is quoted; not cited inline. ‘τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν πολεμουμένων’ rendered ‘those they assail’ (those warred upon by them, i.e. the possessed).

‘the life lived among Hadrian’s favourites’ (wrong: τὰ παιδικά is the role, not a group) made ‘the life lived as the favourite of Hadrian’
φυλάξαντος agrees with Ἀδριανοῦ: the clause now makes Hadrian the one who did not keep the youth free from womanish disorder; note rewritten
σεμνός ‘holy’ made ‘revered’ (keeps ‘holy’ for ἅγιος); ‘since it is said’ made ‘as something said’ (ὡς + participle)
τῶν τυχόντων βρωμάτων ‘certain foods’ made ‘ordinary foods’
Restored the grammar of οἴονται: both the deceived and the conscience-stricken ‘suppose’ they pay a penalty (the deceived group had lost its verb)
Added ‘too’ for καί in ‘the demons too would not withdraw’
